07/04.01.2018 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioners are apprehending, their arrest for the offences under  Sections 11(a) (d) (e) (i) (k) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animal Act 1960, u/s 3  of Animal Slaughter Act 2001, u/s 55 of Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act 2006  and u/s 429/406/188/120(B) of the IPC.
I t i s a l l e g e d t h a t 8 c a m e l s w h i c h w e r e f o u n d u n c l a i m e d a t p u b l i c p l a c e , 
brought for slaughter during Baqrid were seized and entrusted to the petitioners. 
After Baqrid they did not produce the said camels and it has been presumed that  they have slaughtered the camels. 
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that none of the sections of  Prevention of Cruelty to Animal Act is applicable in this case.

He submits that petitioners who had taken entrustment of 2  the camels were duty bound to return the same but by not doing so they have  misappropriated the same.

A f t e r g o i n g t h r o u g h t h e s u b m i s s i o n s o f t h e p a r t i e s a n d a f t e r g o i n g t h r o u g h  records, I find that in A.B.A No. 6352 of 2017 except petitioner no.1 the persons  who were entrusted with camels had not returned the same.
In A.B.A. No. 6503 of  2017 also petitioner no. 1 was also entrusted with camel (which is evident from his  signature at page 27) which he had not returned.

Since the camels entrusted to these  petitioners were not returned, I am not inclined to release the petitioners, namely, 
Ishrafil Rai @ Md. Israfil, Nazir Mian, Munna Ansari @ Munna Mian & Amin Ansari  in A.B.A. No. 6352 of 2017 and petitioner no.1 Akhtar Ansari in A.B.A No. 6503 of 2017.

, I  am inclined to allow their application.
